page: Amazon Web Services c5a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 96 virtual CPUs, corresponding to 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core stress-ng CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, multi-core CPU performance is average. However, the server demonstrates strong capabilities in specific workloads, ranking in the top 10% for PassMark CPU encryption and the top 25% for PassMark CPU score, physics tests, and extended instructions. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong, though large block read and write operations remain average. Software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing benchmarks also place in the top 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the c5a.24xlarge offers a high core count with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio, which is typical for compute-focused hardware classes. This profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for parallelized tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the poor single-core performance, meaning single-threaded applications will experience bottlenecks. Additionally, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may affect I/O-intensive workloads.

This server is suited for highly parallelized, compute-heavy workloads. Appropriate applications include software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and cryptographic operations. It is also capable of handling Redis SET operations and moderate-scale LLM inference prompt processing, though text generation speeds remain average.
